summary: Specifies a SIP extension for reliable provisional responses using the option tag 100rel, and defines the PRACK method that acknowledges them. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Early messages like ringing can get lost. This adds a way for the receiver to say that it got them.

questions: what is a reliable provisional response
subtitle: How SIP gets early 'ringing' style responses delivered reliably, using the 100rel tag and a PRACK acknowledgement.

tldr.problem: SIP sends final responses reliably, but provisional responses (progress messages sent before the final answer) are not sent reliably in RFC 3261. Reliability turned out to matter, including when interoperating with the PSTN.
tldr.mechanism: A provisional response can carry a Require: 100rel header and an RSeq sequence number. The UAS retransmits it with exponential backoff until the caller answers with a new PRACK request whose RAck header names it.
tldr.outcome: SIP gains an optional extension, option tag 100rel, with the PRACK method and the RSeq and RAck headers. It lets session descriptions travel in provisional responses and lets long calls keep proxies from timing out.

today: RFC 3262 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2002. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and it obsoletes RFC 2543.

sections.title: Why Provisional Responses Need Reliability
sections.content:
RFC 3261 defines SIP as a request-response protocol with two kinds of responses. Final responses report the result of a request and are sent reliably. Provisional responses report progress and are not sent reliably in RFC 3261.

The authors note that reliability was later seen to matter in several cases, including interoperability with the PSTN. This RFC therefore adds an optional capability for reliable provisional responses.

The design mirrors how 2xx final responses to INVITE already work. Those are retransmitted by the Transaction User until an ACK arrives. Here, the reliable provisional response is retransmitted with exponential backoff until a PRACK arrives.
sections.eli5: When you phone someone, 'it is ringing' is a small message that can get lost. This RFC lets the phone keep saying it until the other side says 'got it'.

sections.title: How PRACK Mirrors ACK
sections.content:
PRACK plays the same role for provisional responses that ACK plays for 2xx responses, with one important difference. PRACK is a normal SIP request, like BYE. Its own reliability is ensured hop-by-hop through each stateful proxy, and it gets its own response. The RFC says that if this were not so, PRACK could not traverse proxy servers compliant to RFC 2543.

Each reliable provisional response carries a sequence number in the RSeq header field. A PRACK carries an RAck header field naming the response it acknowledges. Acknowledgments are not cumulative, and the specification recommends a single outstanding provisional response at a time for congestion control.
sections.eli5: It works like registered mail. Each message has a number, and the receiver sends back a note saying which number it got.

sections.title: What the Server Does (UAS Behavior)
sections.content:
A UAS MAY send any non-100 provisional response to an INVITE reliably if the INVITE had a Supported header with the option tag 100rel. If the request had a Require header with 100rel, the UAS MUST send every non-100 provisional response reliably, or else reject the request with a 420 (Bad Extension) and an Unsupported header listing 100rel. A 100 (Trying) is never sent reliably, because it is hop-by-hop only; only responses 101 to 199 qualify.

A reliable response MUST include Require: 100rel and an RSeq. The first RSeq value MUST be between 1 and 2**31 - 1, and choosing it uniformly in that range is RECOMMENDED. Later ones MUST be greater by exactly one and MUST NOT wrap around. The response is retransmitted starting at an interval of T1 seconds, doubling each time. Unlike 2xx retransmissions, the interval does not cap at T2.

Retransmission stops when a matching PRACK arrives: same dialog, and a method, CSeq number and response number matching the response. The UAS answers a matching PRACK with a 2xx. A PRACK that matches nothing gets a 481. If the response is retransmitted for 64*T1 seconds with no PRACK, the UAS SHOULD reject the original request with a 5xx.

The UAS MUST NOT send a second reliable provisional response until the first is acknowledged, because the first conveys the initial sequence number. After a final response, it MUST NOT send new reliable provisional responses.
sections.eli5: The sender numbers each early message, keeps repeating it more and more slowly, and stops when it hears 'got number 5'. If nobody ever answers, it gives up.

sections.title: What the Caller Does (UAC Behavior)
sections.content:
A caller can insist on reliable provisional responses by putting Require: 100rel in an INVITE. It MUST NOT put that value in requests other than INVITE, unless a SIP extension allows it. To merely say it supports the feature, it includes Supported: 100rel, and it SHOULD do so in all INVITE requests.

When a provisional response with Require: 100rel arrives, the UAC MUST create a PRACK and send it in the dialog of that response. The response must establish a dialog if none exists yet. A 100 (Trying) with this tag MUST be ignored for this purpose.

The UAC keeps a sequence number of the most recent in-order reliable provisional response, starting from the RSeq of the first one it receives. Retransmissions, recognised by matching dialog ID, CSeq and RSeq, MUST be discarded. If a later reliable response does not have an RSeq exactly one higher, the UAC MUST NOT acknowledge or process it. It MAY discard it or cache it hoping the missing ones arrive.
sections.eli5: The caller sends back a receipt for each numbered message. If it sees number 7 before number 6, it does not send a receipt yet and waits for the missing one.

sections.title: The PRACK Method, RSeq and RAck
sections.content:
The RFC defines one new method, PRACK, and two new header fields.

RSeq appears in provisional responses and holds a single numeric value from 1 to 2**32 - 1. An example is RSeq: 988789.

RAck appears in a PRACK and holds three parts: the RSeq value of the response being acknowledged, then the CSeq number and the method copied from the CSeq of that response. The method name is case sensitive. An example is RAck: 776656 1 INVITE.

The RFC also gives tables extending the SIP header-field tables for PRACK, and a collected BNF for the headers.
sections.eli5: RSeq is the number written on the message. RAck is the receipt that says which number, and which call, it is for.

sections.title: Offer/Answer and Reliable Responses
sections.content:
Because reliable provisional responses and PRACK are dependable, they open new places to exchange session descriptions (offers and answers, per RFC 3264). If the INVITE contained an offer, the UAS MAY put an answer in a reliable provisional response, which sets up the session before the call completes. If the INVITE had no offer, the first reliable provisional response MUST contain one.

A UAC that receives an offer in a reliable provisional response MUST put an answer in the PRACK. If it receives an answer, it MAY put a new offer in the PRACK, and the UAS then MUST put its answer in the 2xx to the PRACK. Once an answer has been sent or received, the UA SHOULD establish the session even if the INVITE has not been answered.

If a reliable provisional response with a session description is still unacknowledged when the INVITE is accepted, the UAS MUST delay the 2xx until it is acknowledged.
sections.eli5: Two people can agree on how to talk, like which language to use, while the phone is still ringing, because the early messages are now safe.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
An attacker can inject a PRACK to make the UAS stop retransmitting a reliable provisional response. Since those responses can carry important information, PRACK messages SHOULD be authenticated like any other request, using the procedures in RFC 3261.

The IANA section registers the option tag 100rel and the header names RSeq and RAck, neither of which has a compact form.
sections.eli5: A trickster could send a fake receipt so the sender stops repeating the message. So receipts should be checked, like any other message.
